To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The polarization resistance Rp, which is the inverse of the corrosion rate, is lower for a sample deformed by a plastic strain in compression than for an undeformed sample.

the Rp value is a good indicator of the corrosion state of carbon steel in sulphuric acid, and that this value decreases when the relative plastic deformation is higher, whatever its sign, and that the Rp value depends on the cutting orientation with regard to the sample axis.

the polarization resistance, which is the inverse of corrosion rate, decreases when the plastic deformation increases and also when the surface orientation is changed from the parallel to the perpendicular one.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanical and electrochemical behaviour of a cast steel.
the study of a carbon steel, elaborated in foundry with a ferrito-pearlito structure, in corrosion in sulphuric acid.

the study of the influence of the hardening state on the electrochemical corrosion behaviour of the steel, and the obtained results show that the Rp value is the most sensitive parameter to this effect.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the corrosion behaviour of a carbon steel, in sulphuric acid, is more sensitive to the mechanical hardening than to the cutting orientation.
the Rp value is more sensitive than the cyclic curves to the mechanical state of the material, and in particular that it is more sensitive to the surface orientation.
the Rp values are more influenced by the surface orientation and the plastic deformation rate, than by the corrosion state change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for the same initial deformation rate, the Rp value is higher for the perpendicular cutting direction, but that, for the two orientations, the Rp value decreases with the increasing of the plastic deformation.
the mechanical properties of this steel are not affected by its corrosion state, while the corrosion state is strongly dependent on the mechanical properties.
the mechanical properties of the cast steel are not significantly affected by corrosion, and conversely, the corrosion behaviour is only slightly affected by the mechanical properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the polarization resistance Rp, and the corrosion rate, can be used to assess, in the case of a cast ferrite-pearlite steel, the mechanical state of the sample surface, which is not the case for the cyclic polarization curves.
the corrosion behaviour of a carbon steel is more sensitive to the plastic deformation state than to the mechanical properties.
the polarization resistance is more sensitive than the cyclic polarization curves to the surface hardening, and therefore, to the mechanical properties of the material.
